reason: The hypothesis relies on five key premises. E3 and E4 directly support improved CO oxidation and stability with configurational disorder in spinel oxides. E5 shows enhanced oxygen vacancies and strong metal–support interactions for a Pd/HEFO catalyst, but this is for Pd, not Pt, and a fluorite, not spinel, structure. No cited evidence addresses Pt nanoparticles on high-entropy spinel supports, the predicted 50% T10 reduction versus Pt/CeO2, or durability under automotive redox cycling. E1 and E2 are about OER electrocatalysis and are irrelevant. Thus, only the first premise is well-supported;
premises: Increasing configurational disorder in spinel oxides improves CO oxidation activity and stability
High-entropy spinel oxides contain abundant oxygen vacancies that facilitate oxygen activation
Strong metal–support interactions in high-entropy oxides anchor noble metal nanoparticles and inhibit sintering
Pt nanoparticles on high-entropy oxide supports will exhibit lower light-off temperatures than Pt/CeO2
The catalyst will maintain superior durability under high-temperature redox cycling
